defect: Cron phase lock: a successful run stores nextAttemptAt = run start + 6 h, but the cron fires at fixed clock times (17 */6 * * *). A tick landing seconds before the due time skipped every vendor; the run saved no observations and did not advance lastRefreshAt, so the refresh cadence drifted from six to twelve hours and the board (stale after 8 h) reported stale for hours between runs.

scenario.fixtureSource: tests/fixtures via vendor-fixtures.mjs; Bank of Israel rate table stubbed for the offline run

currentRun.expression: due <= now + EARLY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS for vendors with consecutiveFailures = 0; strict for backoff

interpretation: Under the pre-fix rule the fixed tick saved 0 observations, so production would not advance lastRefreshAt and the board would report stale for hours between the (now twelve-hourly) refreshes. Under the fixed rule the same tick saves all three vendors and advances the completion marker. The scenario injects past timestamps; the pipeline records finishedAt with the real clock, so lastRefreshAt wall-clock values are not compared here. The deterministic signal is whether any vendor saved an observation, which is exactly the production rule for advancing lastRefreshAt.
